description: Constraints, transaction rollback, savepoints, sequences, and prepared statement SQL surface
sql: CREATE TABLE nm_tx_parent (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, n INT CHECK (n > 0));
CREATE TABLE nm_tx_child (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, parent_code TEXT REFERENCES nm_tx_parent(code) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE SET NULL);
INSERT INTO nm_tx_parent (id, code, n) VALUES ('p1', 'alpha', nextval('nm_tx_seq')::int);
UPDATE nm_tx_parent SET code = 'beta' WHERE id = 'p1';
SELECT parent_code FROM nm_tx_child WHERE id = 'c1';
BEGIN; INSERT INTO nm_tx_parent (id, code, n) VALUES ('rolled', 'rolled', 1); ROLLBACK;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM nm_tx_parent WHERE id = 'rolled';
BEGIN; SAVEPOINT nm_sp; INSERT INTO nm_tx_parent (id, code, n) VALUES ('sp', 'savepoint', 1); ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT nm_sp; COMMIT;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM nm_tx_parent WHERE id = 'sp';
PREPARE nm_plan(text) AS SELECT id FROM nm_tx_parent WHERE code = $1;
expected_difference: Current BicDB parity gaps include CREATE SEQUENCE/nextval, SQL-level PREPARE/EXECUTE, savepoint execution, and some transaction statement batching semantics. These remain explicit intentional gaps until implemented.
